To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
AF-QCN is a new congestion control scheme which is a combination of the QCN algorithm, and the AFB algorithm, and that AF-QCN provides approximate weighted fairness in multi-tenancy environments.
AF-QCN provides: (1) rapid convergence to weighted fairness, (2) a programmable weighted fairness, and (3) good congestion management performance.

(1) we have designed an algorithm that is a fair extension of the QCN algorithm, which is currently being standardized by the IEEE 802 committee; (2) this algorithm is stable and responsive and requires minimal changes to a QCN-capable switch; and (3) the algorithm is capable of providing programmable weighted bandwidth shares to flows or flow-classes.
In summary, our research is concerned with
developing a congestion management algorithm for Data Center Networks, which is simple and easy to implement, and which provides programmable (approximated) weighted fairness.
the design of an approximate fair congestion management algorithm for multi-tenant data centers that is simple to implement, stable, responsive, scalable, and programmable.
the design of congestion control algorithms that are suitable for the data transport needs of multi-tenant Data Center networks.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the AF-QCN algorithm provides a very good trade-off between the simplicity of the QCN algorithm and the programmability of weighted fairness.
the AF-QCN algorithm is an effective way to provide weighted fair bandwidth shares in multi-tenant Data Center environments.
AF-QCN is a very simple and efficient algorithm that can be used for congestion control in multi-tenancy data center environments.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
AF-QCN is a fair, fast, and simple congestion control scheme that can be used to provide fair bandwidth allocation to multiple tenants in a multi-tenanted data center environment.
AF-QCN can be implemented on a QCN-capable switch with no modification, it is stable, it converges rapidly to fairness, and it provides approximate fairness.
we provide the first algorithm to combine the good performance of the IEEE 802.Qau standard (QCN) with approximate fair allocation of bandwidth to flows/flow classes.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the QCN algorithm, which has been adopted by the 802.1 working group for Layer 2 congestion control in Data Center Networks, can be enhanced to provide programmable weighted fairness.
QCN can be used to implement a wide range of fairness objectives in multi-tenancy data centers.
QCN can be used as a building block for more complex congestion management algorithms that provide programmable fairness.
